name: s5_scorecards_slide
title: On the primary scorecard the prediction rules tie or lose to always predicting 'low'
caption: Share of scorecard cells each test got right: filled dots = the pre-registered rules, open diamonds = a predictor that always says 'low' on the same cells; bars are Wilson 95% intervals over cells, numbers at right are correct/cells, dashed line is the declared 0.80 bar. On the primary scorecard (free readouts, shaded) always-low gets 33/38 vs the rules' 31/38 in exp 19 and ties 30/38 in exp 22; exp 18 declared no primary split. Only after dropping the judged Oracle Lens exhibits cell do the rules pull ahead. Per-rule rows are in the backup s5_scorecards.

notes: Computed with g3_s5_scorecards.py's load/aggregates/check_predictions from score18/19/22.json (no re-derivation). Primary = NLA states, NLA complement (multi-choice; pre-registered as 'NLA names the complement', a multi-candidate forced-choice argmax), Oracle Lens exhibits, Oracle Lens states, J-lens on uncued rows (JSON and HTML nesting depth excluded in 19; JSON nesting depth and code language in 22); secondary = the two prompted cells. Wilson intervals treat cells as independent, which they are not (several cells per row), so they are if anything too narrow. Exp 18 rules 44/70 vs always-low 40/70 on all cells: there the rules lead.
